title: Backtesting a whole market in one batch

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You've got a trading idea. Does it work on one stock, or on five hundred?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: BatchBacktesting is built to answer that. It turns a backtest into a repeatable batch, from the AlgoÉTS club.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You pick your instruments, for example the S and P five hundred list pulled from Wikipedia, or a set of crypto pairs. The project downloads daily prices, cleans them, then runs a strategy on every ticker.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In parallel, with a thread pool. For each one it saves a CSV of results, and optionally an interactive HTML chart of the trades.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twenty-three of them, from moving-average crossovers to R S I, MACD and Bollinger Bands. The default is an EMA crossover, where a fast average crossing a slow one triggers a trade, with a stop and a target around it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A notebook ranks the instruments by return and plots the best five against simply buying and holding.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So every step stays visible in Python, not hidden behind a dashboard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the charm. The full write-up has the walkthrough.
